2026 Paris Motor Show • Hyundai Tucson N Line Steals the Spotlight in Paris, but It's All Show and No Go
The Bentley Torcal's Launch Spec Bundles Naim 28-Speaker Audio, Unique Wheels, Carbon Goodies
14 photos
Photo: Bentley
Bentley waited a month after its Torcal electric vehicle's London debut to show off the launch edition. Appropriately called First Edition, this zero-emission luxobarge pairs the most powerful drivetrain with optional equipment such as Mulliner calipers, powered doors, a stupendously nice Naim audio system, and carbon-fiber stylistic touches.
Starting with the dual-motor powertrain, the limited-run Torcal First Edition makes 888 ps ( 876 hp ) and 1,350 Nm (996 lb-ft) of torque. Bentley claims 2.8 seconds to 60 mph (97 kph), while its maximum speed is estimated at 162 mph (260 kph) on summer-only performance rubber.
Truth be told, it's only natural that Bentley chose the high-output version of the Torcal for this edition. As of this writing, the most powerful Torcal yet also doubles as the brand's punchiest road-going model. Crewe wants the first wave of customer orders locked while the debut still has some heat in it, and the First Edition hands those buyers an enticing cocktail of performance and luxury.
From a visual standpoint, First Edition specifics include 22-inch wheels that mix black and Liquid Silver. Self-leveling caps are on the menu, so the winged Bs remain upright while the wheels spin. The unique wheel design is complemented by Graphene Grey brake calipers by Mulliner, namely the in-house personalization arm of the British marque.
Carbon fiber gives a number of parts a sporting look, those parts being the mirror caps, rear aerodynamic diffuser, front bumper winglets, and side sills. While on the subject of exterior goodies, First Edition badging serves as the cherry on top.
Photo: Bentley Opening the door, you're presented with First Edition treadplates that light up, bespoke seat quilting that runs contrasting chevrons, the Frosted Diamond Switchable Sunroof, and 1,780 watts of Naim audio excellence. The 28-speaker configuration includes front headrest speakers and kinaesthetic seat transducers.
What Bentley calls the Colour Specification widens the interior palette with two color splits by Mulliner, the option of a third interior color, and eight accent colors. Gloss Carbon Fibre trim pieces are standard, while alternative finishes come at no additional cost. Of course, deep-pile overmats offer the underfoot plush.
Speaking of plushness, Wellness front seats and the Rear Comfort Seat Specification are the norm here. The rear-seat treatment and the power rear doors indicate a chauffeur-oriented setup, but remember that Bentley never shied from acknowledging that its production models are engaging to drive as well.
Bentley won't say what the launch spec retails for, how many are in the offing, or when first deliveries are due in the automaker's most important of markets. On the other hand, we do know that its 113-kWh battery is good for up to 600 kilometers (375 miles) of WLTP driving range.
Similar under the skin to the Porsche Cayenne Electric, the Torcal is running an 800-volt electrical architecture that supports 400-kW charging. In optimal conditions, DC fast charging from 10 to 80 percent takes less than 20 minutes.
